**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Attorneys at Law*

600 Lexington Avenue New York, New York 10022 Telephone: (212) 554-7000 Facsimile: (212) 554-7001 www.calderwoodharkness.com

January 29, 2024

Ardent Capital Partners III LP c/o Ardent Capital Management LLC 399 Park Avenue, 41st Floor New York, New York 10022

> Attention: Julian Desmond, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> Priya Chandrasekar, Co-Founder & Managing Partner

**Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Antitrust and Hart-Scott-Rodino Advisory Services in Connection with the Acquisition of Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc.**

**Matter No.: 1001-00001**

Dear Mr. Desmond and Ms. Chandrasekar:

**[1. Introduction and Engagement Overview]{.underline}**

We are pleased to confirm that Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"the Firm,\" \"Calderwood & Harkness,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") has been engaged by Ardent Capital Partners III LP (\"Ardent Capital,\" \"Fund III,\" or \"you\"), a Delaware limited partnership, to provide antitrust and competition law advisory services in connection with Ardent Capital\'s proposed acquisition of one hundred percent (100%) of the outstanding equity interests of Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc. (\"Pinnacle\" or \"PHS\"), a Delaware corporation headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. Pinnacle is a specialty healthcare services platform that owns and operates a network of ambulatory surgical centers (\"ASCs\") and physician practice management entities across nine states. Pinnacle\'s operations span a broad geographic footprint, with significant concentrations in the southeastern United States, and the company has established itself as a meaningful participant in the delivery of outpatient surgical and practice management services.

We understand that the proposed transaction is structured as a stock purchase pursuant to which Ardent Capital, through one or more acquisition vehicles, will acquire all of the outstanding shares of common stock and preferred stock of Pinnacle from the current holders thereof, including Veltrano Equity Holdings LLC, certain management stockholders, and other minority equity participants. The enterprise value of Pinnacle for purposes of the proposed transaction is approximately Nine Hundred Fifty-Two Million Dollars (\$952,000,000). An Equity Purchase Agreement (the \"EPA\") reflecting the definitive terms of the proposed acquisition is expected to be executed by the parties on or about January 31, 2024.

We understand that Whitfield & Crane LLP, led by David Ostrander as Lead Partner, is serving as lead transaction counsel to Ardent Capital in connection with the proposed acquisition. Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the antitrust and Hart-Scott-Rodino (\"HSR\") workstream as more fully described in Section 2 below. We look forward to coordinating closely with Mr. Ostrander and his team to ensure that the antitrust workstream proceeds in alignment with the overall transaction timeline and closing conditions.

For the avoidance of doubt, we acknowledge that Ardent Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company registered as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, serves as the registered investment adviser and manager of Fund III, and that Ardent Capital GP III LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, serves as the general partner of Fund III. The relationships among these entities are relevant to the HSR filing analysis, including the determination of the \"Ultimate Parent Entity\" for purposes of the premerger notification, and will be addressed as part of our engagement.

This engagement letter sets forth the terms and conditions of our representation, including the scope of the engagement, the engagement team, our fee arrangements, and other matters relevant to the attorney-client relationship. We ask that you review this letter carefully and confirm your agreement to its terms by executing and returning a countersigned copy as provided in Section 12 below.

**[2. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The Firm\'s engagement encompasses the following services in connection with the proposed acquisition of Pinnacle:

**2.1 HSR Premerger Notification Filing**

The Firm will prepare and file the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act premerger notification form (the \"HSR Form\") on behalf of the acquiring person --- Ardent Capital Partners III LP --- with both the Federal Trade Commission (the \"FTC\") and the Antitrust Division of the United States Department of Justice (the \"DOJ\"). For purposes of the HSR filing, Ardent Capital Management LLC will be identified as the Ultimate Parent Entity (\"UPE\") of the acquiring person, consistent with the Firm\'s analysis of the applicable beneficial ownership and control relationships among Fund III, its general partner, and its investment manager.

As part of the HSR filing process, the Firm will conduct a thorough analysis of the applicable jurisdictional thresholds under the HSR Act and the implementing regulations promulgated by the FTC, as revised for calendar year 2024. Specifically, the Firm will analyze the size-of-transaction threshold, which for 2024 is set at \$111.4 million. Given that the enterprise value of the proposed transaction is approximately \$952 million, the size-of-transaction threshold is clearly exceeded. The Firm will also conduct the size-of-person analysis for both the acquiring person and the acquired person to determine whether the higher filing thresholds are applicable and to confirm the correct filing fee tier.

With respect to filing fees, the Firm has determined on a preliminary basis that the transaction value of approximately \$952 million falls within the \$500 million to \$999.9 million tier under the 2024 FTC fee schedule, resulting in an applicable filing fee of \$280,000. The Firm will confirm this determination upon finalization of the transaction value and prior to submission of the HSR Form.

The Firm will coordinate with Pinnacle\'s antitrust counsel, Greenvale Durneval LLP, led by Jonathan Felder as Lead Partner, to facilitate the simultaneous filing of the acquired person notification form. Timely coordination with target-side counsel is critical to avoid delays in the commencement of the statutory waiting period, and the Firm will work diligently to ensure that both filings are submitted on the same business day.

A central component of the HSR filing preparation will be the identification, collection, and production of documents responsive to Item 4(c) and Item 4(d) of the HSR Form. Item 4(c) requires the production of documents prepared by or for officers or directors of the filing person that analyze the transaction with respect to markets, market shares, competition, competitors, potential for sales growth, or expansion into new product or geographic markets. Item 4(d) requires the production of certain studies, surveys, analyses, and reports that analyze market shares, competition, competitors, or markets for any product or service of the filing person that also relates to products or services of the other party to the transaction. The Firm will work with Ardent Capital\'s deal team and investment professionals to identify all potentially responsive documents, will conduct a thorough privilege review of such documents, and will prepare appropriate redactions and privilege logs as necessary to protect attorney-client privileged and work product materials from disclosure.

**2.2 Early Termination Request**

The Firm will prepare and submit, on behalf of Ardent Capital, a request for early termination of the initial thirty (30) day statutory waiting period under the HSR Act, 15 U.S.C. § 18a(b)(1). Early termination, if granted by both the FTC and the DOJ, would allow the parties to consummate the transaction prior to the expiration of the full thirty-day waiting period, thereby potentially accelerating the closing timeline.

In support of the early termination request, the Firm will prepare a voluntary submission, commonly referred to as a \"white paper,\" for submission to FTC staff in the Premerger Notification Office and the relevant Bureau of Competition division. The white paper will present a detailed substantive competitive analysis of the proposed transaction, including a discussion of the relevant product and geographic markets, the competitive landscape, the absence of meaningful competitive overlaps, and the procompetitive efficiencies anticipated to result from the transaction. The purpose of the white paper is to provide the reviewing agency with sufficient information to conclude that the transaction does not raise competitive concerns warranting further investigation, thereby supporting the grant of early termination or, at minimum, facilitating the smooth expiration of the statutory waiting period without the issuance of a Second Request.

**2.3 Substantive Antitrust Analysis**

The Firm will conduct a comprehensive substantive antitrust analysis of the proposed transaction, addressing the following areas:

**Relevant Product Markets.** The Firm will analyze the relevant product markets implicated by the proposed transaction. Based on our preliminary understanding of Pinnacle\'s operations, the primary relevant product markets are expected to include (i) ambulatory surgical center services, encompassing outpatient surgical procedures performed in freestanding ASC facilities, and (ii) physician practice management services, encompassing the management, administrative support, and operational services provided to physician practices under management services agreements or similar arrangements. The Firm will evaluate the appropriate product market definitions in light of applicable case law, FTC and DOJ enforcement actions in the healthcare sector, and the 2023 Merger Guidelines.

**Relevant Geographic Markets.** The Firm will conduct a Metropolitan Statistical Area (\"MSA\")-level geographic market analysis across Pinnacle\'s nine-state operational footprint, which includes facilities and operations in North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, Tennessee, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Ohio, and Texas. The geographic market analysis will assess the competitive conditions in each MSA in which Pinnacle operates one or more ASCs or manages physician practices, taking into account patient travel patterns, payor contracting dynamics, and referral source characteristics.

**Horizontal Overlap Analysis.** The Firm will analyze potential horizontal competitive overlaps between Pinnacle and Ardent Capital\'s existing healthcare portfolio companies, specifically: (i) Marlowe Asset Management Rehabilitation Holdings LLC (\"Marlowe Asset Management\"), which operates outpatient physical therapy clinics in Texas, Florida, and Georgia; and (ii) Clearpath Diagnostics Inc. (\"Clearpath\"), which provides clinical laboratory services in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and New York. Although the services provided by Marlowe Asset Management (outpatient physical therapy) and Clearpath (clinical laboratory services) are distinct from the services provided by Pinnacle (ASC services and physician practice management), the Firm will assess whether any theory of horizontal competition could be advanced by the reviewing agency, including with respect to any ancillary service lines or overlapping payor relationships.

**HHI Concentration Analysis.** The Firm will calculate Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (\"HHI\") concentration levels for each relevant geographic market in which Pinnacle operates, both pre-transaction and post-transaction, to assess whether the proposed transaction would result in concentration levels or changes in concentration that could raise presumptive competitive concerns under the 2023 Merger Guidelines.

**Vertical Relationships Analysis.** The Firm will analyze potential vertical relationships between Ardent Capital\'s existing portfolio companies and Pinnacle. In particular, the Firm will evaluate referral patterns and referral relationships between Marlowe Asset Management Rehabilitation Holdings LLC\'s physical therapy clinics and Pinnacle\'s ASCs in the three states (Texas, Florida, and Georgia) where both companies maintain operations. The Firm will assess whether any such vertical relationships could give rise to theories of competitive harm, including foreclosure or raising rivals\' costs, and will prepare appropriate responsive analysis.

**Competitor Identification and Market Participant Mapping.** The Firm will identify and map the principal competitors and market participants in each relevant product and geographic market, drawing upon publicly available data, proprietary healthcare industry databases, and information provided by the Ardent Capital deal team. This market participant mapping will support both the HHI analysis and the preparation of the voluntary submission to FTC staff.

**2.4 Regulatory Correspondence and Advocacy**

The Firm will handle all communications with the FTC Bureau of Competition, the Premerger Notification Office, and/or the DOJ Antitrust Division in connection with the HSR filing and the review of the proposed transaction. This includes, without limitation, responses to questions from agency staff regarding the HSR Form, informal requests for additional information or clarification, and any meetings or telephone conferences with agency personnel.

In the event that the FTC or DOJ issues a formal request for additional information and documentary material (a \"Second Request\") pursuant to 15 U.S.C. § 18a(e), the Firm will advise Ardent Capital regarding the scope and implications of the Second Request and the available strategic options. As discussed further in Section 2.6 below, the scope of this engagement would need to be expanded by mutual agreement to encompass Second Request compliance, and the Firm would provide a separate fee estimate for that additional work.

The Firm will coordinate with Greenvale Durneval LLP (target\'s antitrust counsel) and Fendowell Thornton LLP, led by Catherine \"Kate\" Yardley as Lead Partner (counsel to the target/seller, Veltrano Equity Holdings LLC), as required in connection with the filing process, regulatory communications, and any agency review of the proposed transaction. Such coordination may include joint advocacy efforts, information sharing for filing purposes, and alignment on timing and procedural matters.

**2.5 Closing Deliverables**

Upon expiration or early termination of the HSR waiting period, the Firm will prepare an HSR clearance certificate in the form of an officer\'s certificate confirming the expiration or early termination of the applicable HSR waiting period. This certificate will be delivered at closing as required by the Equity Purchase Agreement and will serve as evidence of the satisfaction of the antitrust closing condition.

The Firm will also provide written confirmation of the satisfaction of the antitrust closing condition set forth in Section 6.1(c) of the EPA, including any supporting documentation reasonably required by transaction counsel or the parties in connection with the closing.

**2.6 Scope Limitations**

It is important that the scope of this engagement be clearly understood. This engagement does **not** include representation of Ardent Capital with respect to the negotiation, drafting, or documentation of the Equity Purchase Agreement or any ancillary transaction documents; debt financing, including any credit facilities, commitment letters, or related arrangements; tax structuring, planning, or advisory services; employment, benefits, or compensation matters; intellectual property due diligence, prosecution, or licensing; real estate due diligence, title, survey, or environmental matters; or any other legal workstream not directly related to the antitrust and HSR matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above.

This engagement also does **not** include representation of Ardent Capital before any state antitrust authority or in connection with any state-level merger notification requirements that may be applicable to the proposed transaction, unless separately agreed in writing between the Firm and Ardent Capital. If state-level filings or approvals are required, the Firm would be pleased to discuss the scope of any additional engagement on mutually agreeable terms.

If a Second Request is issued by the FTC or DOJ in connection with the proposed transaction, the scope of this engagement will be expanded by mutual written agreement between the Firm and Ardent Capital. In such event, the Firm will promptly provide Ardent Capital with a separate scope of work and fee estimate for Second Request compliance, including any necessary document collection, custodian interviews, data submissions, and advocacy before the reviewing agency. Second Request compliance engagements typically involve substantially greater time, resources, and expense, and it is therefore important that the parties agree in advance on the scope and fee arrangements for any such expanded engagement.

**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys have been assigned to this engagement and will be principally responsible for the delivery of the services described in Section 2:

**Howard Bellamy** --- *Responsible Partner and Billing Partner, Antitrust & Competition Practice Group.* Mr. Bellamy is a partner in the Firm\'s Antitrust & Competition Practice Group and has extensive experience advising private equity sponsors, strategic acquirors, and other clients on HSR filings, merger clearance, and antitrust regulatory matters across a wide range of industries, including healthcare services. Mr. Bellamy will serve as the primary relationship partner for Ardent Capital and will have overall responsibility for the strategic direction, quality, and supervision of the engagement. Mr. Bellamy will personally participate in all material communications with the reviewing agency and will lead any advocacy efforts before the FTC or DOJ.

**Monica Reyes** --- *Lead Associate, Antitrust & Competition Practice Group.* Ms. Reyes is a senior associate in the Firm\'s Antitrust & Competition Practice Group with particular expertise in HSR premerger notification filings and healthcare antitrust matters. Ms. Reyes will have day-to-day responsibility for the preparation of the HSR filing, supervision of the Item 4(c) and Item 4(d) document collection and review process, and drafting of the substantive antitrust analysis memoranda and the voluntary submission (white paper) to FTC staff.

**Elliot Nguyen** --- *Working Associate, Antitrust & Competition Practice Group.* Mr. Nguyen is an associate in the Firm\'s Antitrust & Competition Practice Group. Mr. Nguyen will assist with market research, HHI concentration calculations, regulatory analysis, NAICS code identification, competitor mapping, and document review. Mr. Nguyen will work under the supervision of Mr. Bellamy and Ms. Reyes.

Additional attorneys, paralegals, or staff may be assigned to this engagement as necessary to ensure the timely and efficient delivery of services. The Firm will provide prior notice to Ardent Capital of any additional personnel assigned to the matter, along with the applicable billing rates for such personnel.

**[4. Fees and Billing Arrangements]{.underline}**

**4.1 Hourly Rates**

The Firm will bill for its services on an hourly basis. The Firm\'s current standard hourly rates for the attorneys assigned to this matter are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper**          **Title**               **Hourly Rate**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Howard Bellamy          Partner                 \$1,650

  Monica Reyes            Senior Associate        \$875

  Elliot Nguyen           Associate               \$725
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

In the event that additional attorneys or paralegals are assigned to the engagement, their applicable hourly rates will be communicated to Ardent Capital at the time of assignment. Paralegal rates at the Firm currently range from \$350 to \$475 per hour, depending on the seniority and experience of the paralegal.

The hourly rates set forth above are the Firm\'s standard rates for calendar year 2024. Hourly rates are subject to annual adjustment, which typically takes effect on January 1 of each year. Any rate adjustments applicable to this engagement for calendar year 2025 or thereafter will be communicated to Ardent Capital in advance of their effective date. Given our current expectation that this engagement will be completed within the first half of 2024, we do not anticipate that any rate adjustments will apply during the course of this engagement.

**4.2 Billing Cycle and Payment Terms**

Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered on a monthly basis, typically within fifteen (15) business days following the end of each calendar month. All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. The Firm reserves the right to charge interest on past due amounts at the rate of one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less.

Each invoice will include a detailed description of the services rendered during the billing period, the identity of each timekeeper who performed services, the number of hours worked by each timekeeper, the applicable hourly rate, and the total fees for the period. All invoices will reference Matter No. 1001-00001 and should be directed to the attention of the Ardent Capital finance or accounting team at the address set forth above, or to such other address or electronic billing system as Ardent Capital may designate in writing.

**4.3 Expenses and Disbursements**

In addition to professional fees, Ardent Capital will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses and disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with this engagement. Such expenses and disbursements may include, but are not limited to, the following: filing fees (including the HSR filing fee); overnight delivery and courier charges; travel expenses (including airfare, hotel, ground transportation, and meals) incurred in connection with meetings with the FTC or DOJ or other engagement-related travel; copying, printing, and scanning costs; charges for online legal research services (such as Westmark Data Systems, Calderon Systems, and Cascade Services Inc.); messenger services; and long-distance telephone charges. All expenses will be billed at cost, without markup, and will be itemized on the applicable monthly invoice.

With respect to the HSR filing fee, the Firm has determined on a preliminary basis that the applicable filing fee for the proposed transaction is \$280,000, based on a transaction value of approximately \$952 million falling within the \$500 million to \$999.9 million tier under the 2024 FTC fee schedule. This filing fee will be paid directly by Ardent Capital to the FTC through the FTC\'s electronic filing system, consistent with Ardent Capital\'s obligation under Section 5.4(a) of the Equity Purchase Agreement. Alternatively, if requested by Ardent Capital, the Firm may advance the filing fee on the client\'s behalf, in which case Ardent Capital shall promptly reimburse the Firm upon receipt of an invoice reflecting the advanced amount. The Firm will coordinate with Ardent Capital\'s finance team to determine the preferred approach for payment of the filing fee.

**4.4 Fee Estimate**

Based on our current understanding of the proposed transaction, the anticipated scope of the antitrust and HSR workstream, and the assumption that no Second Request is issued by the FTC or DOJ, the Firm estimates that total professional fees for this engagement will be in the range of **\$125,000 to \$200,000**, exclusive of the \$280,000 HSR filing fee and other out-of-pocket expenses and disbursements. This estimate reflects the Firm\'s assessment of the work likely required to prepare and file the HSR Form, conduct the substantive antitrust analysis, prepare the voluntary submission (white paper), manage regulatory communications with the reviewing agency, and deliver the closing deliverables described in Section 2.5.

This fee estimate is provided for budgeting and planning purposes only and does **not** constitute a cap, fixed fee, or guaranteed maximum fee for this engagement. Actual fees will depend on a number of factors, including the complexity of the competitive analysis, the volume of Item 4(c) and Item 4(d) responsive documents, the nature and extent of any agency inquiries or information requests, and the degree of coordination required with other counsel. If at any time during the engagement it appears that actual fees are likely to materially exceed the upper end of this estimate, the Firm will promptly notify Ardent Capital and discuss the anticipated scope and cost of the remaining work.

**[5. Client Identity and Relationship]{.underline}**

The Firm\'s client in this engagement is Ardent Capital Partners III LP. The attorney-client relationship established by this engagement letter exists solely between the Firm and Fund III.

The Firm does **not** represent, and this engagement does **not** extend to, any of the following: Ardent Capital Management LLC (except in its capacity as the entity identified as the Ultimate Parent Entity for HSR filing purposes); Ardent Capital GP III LLC; any affiliate, subsidiary, or portfolio company of Ardent Capital, including without limitation Marlowe Asset Management Rehabilitation Holdings LLC and Clearpath Diagnostics Inc.; any individual partner, member, officer, director, employee, or agent of any of the foregoing entities; Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc.; Veltrano Equity Holdings LLC; or any other party to the proposed transaction. If any such entity or individual requires separate legal representation in connection with the proposed transaction or any related matter, such representation would need to be established pursuant to a separate engagement letter, subject to the Firm\'s conflicts review and acceptance procedures.

Instructions and direction regarding this engagement may be provided by Julian Desmond and/or Priya Chandrasekar, or their designated representatives, on behalf of Ardent Capital. The Firm will be entitled to rely on instructions received from Mr. Desmond or Ms. Chandrasekar (or their designees) as having been duly authorized by Ardent Capital, unless and until Ardent Capital notifies the Firm in writing to the contrary.

**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

All communications between the Firm and Ardent Capital, and all work product prepared by the Firm in connection with this engagement, will be treated as confidential and, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, will be protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. The Firm recognizes the sensitive and proprietary nature of the information that may be shared with the Firm in connection with this engagement, including information relating to Ardent Capital\'s investment strategy, portfolio company operations, financial projections, and competitive positioning.

The Firm will not disclose confidential information received from or on behalf of Ardent Capital to any third party without Ardent Capital\'s prior written consent, except as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or as necessary in connection with the HSR filing and related governmental submissions made to the FTC and/or the DOJ. In the event the Firm receives a subpoena, court order, or other compulsory process requiring the disclosure of confidential information relating to this engagement, the Firm will, to the extent permitted by applicable law, promptly notify Ardent Capital and cooperate with Ardent Capital in seeking appropriate protective relief.

To the extent that information is shared with Greenvale Durneval LLP (target\'s antitrust counsel), Fendowell Thornton LLP (seller\'s counsel), or other counsel in connection with the coordinated HSR filing process, the Firm will use reasonable efforts to limit such sharing to non-privileged, factual information necessary for filing coordination and regulatory compliance, unless Ardent Capital provides broader written authorization for the sharing of privileged or otherwise confidential information. The Firm will consult with Ardent Capital before entering into any joint defense, common interest, or information-sharing agreements with such other counsel.

**[7. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

The Firm has conducted a conflicts check in connection with this proposed engagement in accordance with its standard conflicts clearance procedures and the applicable provisions of the New York Rules of Professional Conduct. Based on the information currently available to the Firm, including the identities of the parties to the proposed transaction, their affiliates, and the key individuals involved, the Firm has not identified any conflicts of interest that would preclude our representation of Ardent Capital in this matter. A memorandum documenting the results of the Firm\'s internal conflicts review, dated January 28, 2024, has been prepared and is maintained in the Firm\'s conflicts records.

If at any time during the course of this engagement a conflict of interest arises or is identified --- whether as a result of the Firm\'s acceptance of a new client engagement, a change in the circumstances of this engagement, or otherwise --- the Firm will promptly notify Ardent Capital and discuss the appropriate course of action. Depending on the nature and severity of the conflict, the Firm and Ardent Capital may agree to address the conflict through the execution of an informed written waiver by the affected parties, or, if the conflict cannot be appropriately waived, through the Firm\'s withdrawal from the engagement and the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel.

**[8. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Upon completion of this engagement, the Firm will retain client files, work product, and related materials in accordance with the Firm\'s standard document retention policy, which currently provides for the retention of closed matter files for a period of ten (10) years following the date of matter closure. During the retention period, the Firm will maintain the files in a secure manner consistent with its obligations of confidentiality and data security.

Original documents provided to the Firm by Ardent Capital in connection with this engagement, as well as original filing receipts, agency correspondence, and other original materials generated in the course of the engagement, will be returned to Ardent Capital upon request or retained in the Firm\'s files at the client\'s direction. If Ardent Capital does not request the return of original documents, such documents will be retained and ultimately disposed of in accordance with the Firm\'s standard retention policy.

The Firm reserves the right to destroy client files and related materials after the expiration of the applicable retention period, unless Ardent Capital instructs the Firm in writing to retain such files for a longer period. The Firm will make reasonable efforts to provide advance notice to Ardent Capital before destroying any files relating to this engagement, but the Firm shall have no liability for the destruction of files following the expiration of the retention period in the absence of a written instruction to the contrary.

**[9. Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**

To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the Firm\'s aggregate liability to Ardent Capital and any other person or entity in connection with this engagement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total amount of professional fees actually paid by Ardent Capital to the Firm for services rendered under this engagement letter. This limitation of liability applies to any and all claims, losses, damages, costs, and expenses arising out of or relating to the Firm\'s performance or non-performance of the services contemplated by this engagement letter.

In no event shall the Firm be liable to Ardent Capital or any other person or entity for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages of any kind, including without limitation lost profits, lost business opportunities, diminution in value, or any other damages not constituting direct, actual damages, regardless of whether such damages are foreseeable and regardless of whether the Firm has been advised of the possibility of such damages.

Nothing in this Section 9 shall limit or exclude the Firm\'s liability for fraud, willful misconduct, or any liability that cannot be limited or excluded as a matter of applicable law or professional regulation.

**[10. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time, with or without cause, upon written notice to the other party. Written notice of termination may be delivered by email, overnight courier, or certified mail to the applicable address set forth in this engagement letter, or to such other address as either party may designate in writing.

Upon termination of this engagement, Ardent Capital shall remain responsible for the payment of all professional fees and disbursements incurred by the Firm through the date of termination, in accordance with the fee and billing arrangements set forth in Section 4. The Firm will render a final invoice within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination, and payment of such final invoice shall be due in accordance with the payment terms set forth in Section 4.2.

In the event of termination, the Firm will cooperate with Ardent Capital in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel, including the prompt transfer of client files, work product, and other materials, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies of such materials for its records and as required by applicable law and professional regulations. The Firm\'s obligations under Sections 6 (Confidentiality), 9 (Limitation of Liability), and 11 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution) shall survive the termination of this engagement.

**[11. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**

This engagement letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without regard to principles of conflicts of law that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this engagement letter or the Firm\'s provision of services hereunder, including without limitation any dispute regarding the interpretation, validity, enforceability, or termination of this engagement letter, or any claim for breach of fiduciary duty, malpractice, or other professional liability, shall be resolved by binding arbitration in New York, New York, administered by the American Arbitration Association (the \"AAA\") in accordance with the AAA\'s then-current Commercial Arbitration Rules. The arbitration shall be conducted before a single arbitrator selected in accordance with the AAA\'s rules. The arbitrator\'s award shall be final and binding on the parties and may be entered as a judgment in any court of competent jurisdiction. Each party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees in connection with any arbitration proceeding, unless the arbitrator determines that the prevailing party is entitled to recover its reasonable costs and fees from the non-prevailing party.

**[12. Acceptance and Execution]{.underline}**

We are grateful for the opportunity to serve as antitrust counsel to Ardent Capital in connection with this important transaction. We trust that the terms set forth in this engagement letter accurately reflect our mutual understanding and agreement regarding the scope and terms of the Firm\'s representation.

We kindly request that Ardent Capital confirm its acceptance of the terms of this engagement letter by having an authorized representative of Ardent Capital execute the countersignature block below and return a signed copy of this letter to the undersigned at the address set forth above or by email to hbellamy@calderwoodharkness.com. The Firm may commence work upon receipt of the executed engagement letter.

If Ardent Capital does not object to the terms of this engagement letter in writing within fifteen (15) days of the date hereof, the terms set forth in this engagement letter shall be deemed accepted by Ardent Capital.

This engagement letter, together with any exhibits and attachments hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the Firm and Ardent Capital with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous understandings, agreements, representations, and warranties, whether written or oral, with respect thereto.

We look forward to working with you and your team on this matter.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** 900 Third Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022

March 15, 2021

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL

Mr. Marcus Yuen Managing Partner Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP 388 Embarcadero Center, Suite 2400 San Francisco, California 94111

**Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Initial Public Offering of Pinnacle Acquisition Corp. I**

Dear Mr. Yuen:

We are pleased to confirm that Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") has been engaged by Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (\"Pinnacle\" or the \"Sponsor\"), and Pinnacle Acquisition Corp. I, a Delaware corporation (the \"Company\" and, together with the Sponsor, the \"Clients\"), to serve as issuer\'s counsel in connection with the proposed initial public offering (the \"IPO\") of units of the Company (the \"Transaction\"). This letter sets forth the terms and conditions of the engagement, and we ask that you review them carefully. We understand that this is one of the Firm\'s earliest engagements for Pinnacle, and we greatly appreciate the opportunity to work with you and your team. We look forward to bringing the full depth of our capital markets practice to bear on behalf of the Clients and to building a lasting professional relationship.

The terms and conditions governing our representation are set forth below.

**[1. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

Our representation of the Clients in connection with the Transaction will include, but not be limited to, the following:

> **(a) Registration Statement.** Preparation and filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") of a Registration Statement on Form S-1 (including any and all amendments and supplements thereto) under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"), relating to the IPO of up to 20,000,000 units (plus up to 3,000,000 additional units that may be issued pursuant to an over-allotment option granted to the underwriters) at an anticipated offering price of \$10.00 per unit, for aggregate gross proceeds of up to \$230,000,000. Our work in connection with the Registration Statement will include the preparation and submission of an initial confidential draft of the Registration Statement to the SEC pursuant to the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of 2012, as well as any subsequent confidential draft submissions and the eventual public filing of the Registration Statement on EDGAR. We will prepare the Company\'s responses to any SEC staff comment letters received in connection with the review of the Registration Statement, coordinate the preparation of all pre-effective amendments, and advise the Clients on the SEC\'s review process through effectiveness of the Registration Statement.
>
> **(b) Underwriting Agreement.** Drafting and negotiation of the Underwriting Agreement between the Company and Ridgeline Whitfield Securities LLC, as representative of the several underwriters (including Halyard Capital Markets Inc., as co-manager of the offering), relating to the offer and sale of the units in the IPO. The Underwriting Agreement is expected to provide, among other things, for an upfront underwriting discount of 2.0% of the gross proceeds of the IPO and a deferred underwriting commission of 3.5% of the gross proceeds of the IPO, with the deferred underwriting commission to be deposited in the trust account and payable to the underwriters only upon the Company\'s consummation of an initial business combination.
>
> **(c) Investment Management Trust Agreement.** Drafting of the Investment Management Trust Agreement between the Company and Continental Dunmore Financial, as trustee, governing the establishment, maintenance, and administration of the trust account into which the net proceeds of the IPO (at least \$10.00 per public share sold in the IPO) will be deposited and held pending the Company\'s consummation of an initial business combination or the liquidation and distribution of the trust account in accordance with its terms.
>
> **(d) Warrant Agreement.** Drafting of the Warrant Agreement between the Company and Continental Dunmore Financial, as warrant agent, covering the public warrants included as a component of the units sold in the IPO and the private placement warrants to be purchased by the Sponsor simultaneously with the consummation of the IPO, including all terms related to exercise, adjustment, and redemption of such warrants.
>
> **(e) Letter Agreement (Insider Lock-Up).** Drafting of a Letter Agreement (containing insider lock-up and transfer restriction provisions) among the Company, the Sponsor, and each of the Company\'s officers and directors --- specifically, Marcus Yuen, Deborah Sinclair, Raymond Holtz, Nadia Petrova, and William K. Ashmore --- providing for, among other things, restrictions on the transfer of the founder shares and private placement warrants held by such persons until specified periods following the consummation of an initial business combination.
>
> **(f) Registration Rights Agreement.** Drafting of a Registration Rights Agreement among the Company, the Sponsor, and certain security holders, which will provide demand and piggyback registration rights with respect to the founder shares, private placement warrants, and any shares of common stock underlying such securities, and will contain customary terms regarding indemnification and participation rights.
>
> **(g) Corporate Organizational Documents.** Preparation of the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and the Amended and Restated Bylaws of the Company, each to be adopted in connection with the IPO and filed (in the case of the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation) with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. These documents will contain customary provisions for a blank-check company, including provisions relating to the trust account, shareholder redemption rights, the business combination deadline, and the classification of the board of directors.
>
> **(h) Legal Opinions.** Delivery of customary legal opinions and a 10b-5 negative assurance letter (commonly referred to as a \"comfort\" or \"disclosure\" letter) addressed to the underwriters, in connection with the closing of the IPO and, if applicable, at any subsequent closing in connection with the exercise of the over-allotment option. In addition, we will prepare and deliver a tax opinion regarding the federal income tax treatment of the units (and the components thereof) for inclusion in, or filing as an exhibit to, the Registration Statement.
>
> **(i) Closing Deliverables.** Preparation of closing deliverables customary for transactions of this nature, including, without limitation, officer\'s certificates, secretary\'s certificates, good standing certificates, incumbency certificates, and a comprehensive closing checklist and closing set.
>
> **(j) General Advice.** General corporate and securities law advice in connection with the IPO, including advice relating to the Company\'s application for listing of the units, shares of Class A common stock, and warrants on the Nasdaq Capital Market (anticipated ticker symbols: PNACU for units, PNAC for shares of Class A common stock, and PNACW for warrants), coordination with the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (\"FINRA\") in connection with its review of the underwriting terms and arrangements, and advice regarding blue sky matters and state securities law compliance as may be necessary or appropriate.
>
> **(k) Coordination with Other Advisors.** Coordination with the various other professional advisors engaged in connection with the Transaction, including (i) underwriters\' counsel, Whitmore & Caldwell LLP (contact: Garrett Doyle), (ii) the Company\'s Delaware counsel, Beckett & Hale LLP (contact: Amanda Chisholm), (iii) the Company\'s independent registered public accounting firm, Trask, Worthington & Giordano LLP (contact: Sean Novotny), and (iv) Continental Dunmore Financial, as trustee and warrant agent. We will work closely with each of these advisors to facilitate an efficient and coordinated transaction process.

**Scope Exclusion.** The Clients acknowledge and agree that this engagement does not include, and the Firm has not been engaged to provide, legal services in connection with any post-IPO business combination transaction (a \"de-SPAC transaction\"), which engagement, if desired by the Clients, would be the subject of a separate engagement letter to be negotiated and executed at such time. This engagement also does not include the representation of the Clients in connection with the Company\'s ongoing reporting obligations under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the \"Exchange Act\"), following the consummation of the IPO, unless separately agreed to in writing by the Firm and the Clients. Furthermore, this engagement does not include the provision of any state or local tax advice, advice regarding the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or any employment law advice. The Clients should retain separate counsel to the extent that they require legal services in any of these areas.

**[2. Dual Representation; Identity of Clients]{.underline}**

The Clients acknowledge that C&H has been engaged to represent, and is simultaneously representing, both Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the Sponsor) and Pinnacle Acquisition Corp. I (the Company) in connection with this engagement. At this stage of the Transaction (prior to the Company\'s consummation of an initial business combination), the interests of the Sponsor and the Company are closely aligned. The Sponsor formed and controls the Company through Pinnacle Venture Management II LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, which serves as the general partner of the Sponsor. The Company was incorporated in the State of Delaware on January 22, 2021 (Delaware Secretary of State File No. 7319284; Employer Identification Number: 86-3194507) and is a blank-check company formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, capital stock exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization, or similar business combination with one or more businesses.

The Clients understand that, should circumstances arise in which the interests of the Sponsor and the Company materially diverge or become adverse to one another --- for example, in connection with the negotiation or consummation of a future business combination, or in connection with any dispute between the Sponsor and the Company regarding the terms of the founder shares or other arrangements --- C&H will be required to reassess whether continued dual representation is appropriate under the applicable rules of professional conduct. In such circumstances, C&H may recommend, or may be required, to withdraw from the representation of one or both of the Clients and may recommend that one or both of the Clients retain independent counsel. We will endeavor to raise any such issues promptly if and when they arise.

By executing this engagement letter, each of the Clients provides its informed consent, in accordance with Rule 1.7 of the New York Rules of Professional Conduct, to C&H\'s concurrent representation of both the Sponsor and the Company in connection with this engagement, having been afforded the opportunity to consult with independent counsel regarding the implications of such dual representation.

**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys will have primary responsibility for the engagement:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Attorney**                 **Role**                **Practice Group**
  ---------------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Jennifer Kwon, Partner       Responsible Partner     Capital Markets

  Theodore Langston, Partner   Billing Partner         Capital Markets

  Claire Dempsey, Associate    Lead Associate          Capital Markets

  Audrey Zhou, Associate       Working Associate       Capital Markets
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Other attorneys and paraprofessionals of the Firm may assist from time to time as needed, depending on the particular requirements of the engagement and the availability of the engagement team. Jennifer Kwon will serve as the primary point of contact for the Clients with respect to all matters relating to this engagement and should be contacted in the first instance with any questions, instructions, or communications regarding the Transaction. Ms. Kwon can be reached at (212) 555-8400 or jennifer.kwon@calderwoodharkness.com.

**[4. Fees and Expenses]{.underline}**

> **(a) Hourly Rates.** Fees for legal services rendered in connection with this engagement will be based upon the time spent by attorneys and paraprofessionals at their standard hourly rates, which are established by the Firm and are intended to reflect the experience, skill, and expertise of each individual professional. The current standard hourly rates applicable to the professionals expected to work on this engagement are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Professional Category**           **Hourly Rate Range**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Partners                            \$1,050 -- \$1,350

  Counsel                             \$875 -- \$1,050

  Associates                          \$575 -- \$925

  Paraprofessionals                   \$250 -- \$425
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

> These rates are subject to periodic adjustment, typically on an annual basis at or around the beginning of each calendar year. The Clients will be notified of any changes to the applicable hourly rates. To the extent any rate adjustment takes effect during the course of this engagement, the adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of such adjustment.
>
> **(b) Fee Estimate.** Based on the Firm\'s current understanding of the scope of the Transaction and our experience with comparable initial public offerings of special purpose acquisition companies, total legal fees for this engagement are estimated not to exceed \$750,000, exclusive of disbursements. The Clients should understand that this figure is an estimate only and does not constitute a fixed fee, flat fee, or fee cap. The Firm will endeavor to notify the Clients promptly if it appears that total fees will materially exceed this estimate. The actual fees incurred will depend upon a number of factors, many of which are outside the Firm\'s control, including without limitation the number, nature, and complexity of SEC staff comment letters received in connection with the review of the Registration Statement, the extent and complexity of negotiations with the underwriters and their counsel regarding the terms of the Underwriting Agreement and other transaction documents, any changes to the deal structure or offering terms, and the overall pace and timeline of the Transaction.
>
> **(c) Disbursements.** In addition to legal fees, the Clients will be responsible for reimbursing the Firm for all disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with this engagement, including but not limited to SEC filing fees, printing costs, travel expenses, EDGAR filing agent fees, messenger and courier services, long-distance telephone charges, and similar costs. All disbursements will be billed at the Firm\'s actual cost. The SEC registration fee payable in connection with the filing of the Registration Statement is anticipated to be approximately \$23,475, based on a maximum aggregate offering price of \$230,000,000 (calculated as \$200,000,000 for the base offering plus \$30,000,000 for the over-allotment option), using the then-current SEC fee rate of approximately \$0.0001091 per dollar of the maximum aggregate offering price, subject to adjustment per the SEC\'s published fee schedule. EDGAR filing and financial printing services will be provided by Donnovan Financial Printers Inc. and will be billed directly to the Company or, in the event such costs are initially paid by C&H on the Company\'s behalf, passed through to the Clients at cost without markup.
>
> **(d) Billing and Payment Terms.** The Firm will render invoices on a monthly basis, at the end of each calendar month during which legal services are performed or disbursements are incurred. Each invoice will set forth a summary description of the services rendered, the identity of the professionals who performed such services, the hours worked, and the applicable hourly rates, together with an itemization of any disbursements. Payment of each invoice is due within thirty (30) days of the date of the invoice. In the event of any billing inquiry or dispute, the Clients should contact Theodore Langston, the billing partner, promptly upon receipt of the invoice. Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the Sponsor) shall be primarily responsible for the payment of all fees and expenses incurred in connection with this engagement. The Company shall be jointly and severally liable with the Sponsor for the payment of all such fees and expenses.

**[5. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

C&H has conducted a conflicts of interest check in accordance with its standard procedures, which check was completed on March 11, 2021. Based on the results of that check, the Firm has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude this engagement under the New York Rules of Professional Conduct.

In the interest of full transparency, the Firm wishes to disclose the following prior representations that involved parties who will participate in the Transaction:

> \(i\) The Firm has previously represented Ridgeline Whitfield Securities LLC --- which will act as lead underwriter and representative of the several underwriters in this Transaction --- on certain unrelated matters that have been concluded and are now closed. Ridgeline Whitfield will be a counterparty to the Company in connection with the Underwriting Agreement, and Ridgeline Whitfield will be separately represented in this Transaction by its own counsel. No current representation of Ridgeline Whitfield by the Firm exists, and no adverse representation of the Clients against Ridgeline Whitfield is contemplated.
>
> \(ii\) The Firm has also previously represented Continental Dunmore Financial --- which will serve as trustee under the Investment Management Trust Agreement and as warrant agent under the Warrant Agreement --- on an unrelated trust indenture matter that has been concluded and is now closed. Continental Dunmore Financial\'s role in this Transaction is ministerial in nature, and no current representation of Continental Dunmore Financial by the Firm exists.

No other potential conflicts were identified with respect to Halyard Capital Markets Inc., Whitmore & Caldwell LLP, Beckett & Hale LLP, Trask, Worthington & Giordano LLP, or any of the Company\'s officers and directors (Marcus Yuen, Deborah Sinclair, Raymond Holtz, Nadia Petrova, and William K. Ashmore).

The Clients acknowledge and agree that the Firm\'s representation of the Clients in this matter does not preclude the Firm from representing, or continuing to represent, other clients (including clients that may have interests adverse to the Clients) in matters that are unrelated to this engagement, including, without limitation, other clients in the financial services, technology, and capital markets sectors in which the Clients or their affiliates operate. The Firm undertakes not to represent any other party in this specific Transaction in a manner that is adverse to the Clients\' interests in the Transaction without first obtaining the Clients\' prior written consent.

**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

C&H will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by the Clients in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations and applicable rules of professional conduct. Confidential information received from the Clients will not be disclosed to third parties except (a) to Firm personnel (including attorneys, paraprofessionals, administrative staff, and outside service providers operating under obligations of confidentiality) who are working on the engagement and who have a need to know such information, (b) as authorized by the Clients, including disclosure to other parties to the Transaction (such as the underwriters, the auditors, the trustee, Delaware counsel, and their respective representatives) as is necessary or appropriate to consummate the IPO, and (c) as required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or ethical obligation.

The Clients further acknowledge that certain information provided to the Firm in connection with this engagement will be publicly disclosed in the Registration Statement, the Prospectus, and other filings made with the SEC, as required by the Securities Act and the rules and regulations of the SEC. The Firm\'s obligation of confidentiality shall not extend to information that has been made publicly available through such filings or otherwise.

**[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**

The Firm\'s file-retention policy provides for the retention of engagement files (including both paper and electronic files) for a period of ten (10) years following the conclusion of the matter, as determined by the closing of the Firm\'s file for the engagement. After the expiration of such ten-year retention period, the Firm may destroy or dispose of the engagement files, or any portion thereof, without further notice to, or consent from, the Clients. The Firm shall have no obligation to retain any files beyond the ten-year retention period.

The Clients are encouraged to maintain their own complete copies of all important documents, correspondence, and work product generated in connection with this engagement. Electronically stored information will be retained and managed in accordance with the Firm\'s electronic records management policies, which are designed to comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements regarding the preservation and management of electronic records.

**[8. Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**

To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the New York Rules of Professional Conduct, the aggregate liability of the Firm and its partners, counsel, associates, and other personnel to the Clients arising out of, or in any way relating to, the legal services provided under this engagement (whether such liability arises in contract, tort, or otherwise) shall not exceed the total amount of fees actually paid by the Clients to the Firm in connection with this engagement. This limitation of liability applies to all claims and all theories of recovery, including, without limitation, claims for negligence, breach of fiduciary duty, breach of contract, and any statutory claims.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, this limitation of liability shall not apply to any losses, damages, or liabilities that are finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction or an arbitrator (as applicable) to have arisen from the Firm\'s willful misconduct or fraud.

**[9. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time, with or without cause, by providing written notice to the other party. In the case of a termination by the Clients, such notice should be directed to Jennifer Kwon at the address set forth above. In the case of a termination by the Firm, notice will be provided to the Clients at the addresses set forth in this letter or at such other address as the Clients may subsequently designate in writing.

Upon termination of this engagement, the Clients shall remain obligated to pay all fees for services rendered and all disbursements incurred through the effective date of termination. Any unpaid amounts shall be due and payable in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 4 of this letter.

Following any termination, C&H will cooperate reasonably with the Clients in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Clients, including by making available copies of relevant files and work product (subject to the Firm\'s retention of one copy for its own records and subject to payment of all outstanding fees and expenses), all in accordance with applicable ethical rules and professional obligations.

**[10. Governing Law; Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**

This engagement letter shall be governed by, and construed and interpreted in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-laws rules or provisions that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this engagement letter, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered in New York, New York, in accordance with the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association then in effect, before a single arbitrator selected in accordance with such rules, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to an alternative dispute resolution mechanism. The arbitrator\'s award shall be final and binding and may be entered as a judgment in any court of competent jurisdiction. Each party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees incurred in connection with any such arbitration, unless the arbitrator determines that the circumstances warrant a different allocation.

**[11. Entire Agreement; Amendments]{.underline}**

This engagement letter constitutes the entire agreement between the Firm and the Clients with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, representations, understandings, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to the terms and conditions of the Firm\'s engagement by the Clients in connection with the Transaction.

This engagement letter may not be amended, modified, supplemented, or waived except by a written instrument signed by the Firm and each of the Clients. No oral agreement or understanding shall modify or affect the terms of this letter.

**[12. Counterparts]{.underline}**

This engagement letter may be executed in one or more counterparts (including by means of electronic signature delivered via Brightwater Software, Ashford Health IT, or portable document format (PDF) transmitted by electronic mail), each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. A signed copy of this engagement letter delivered by electronic transmission shall have the same legal effect as delivery of an original signed copy.

We would appreciate it if you would review the foregoing terms carefully and, if they accurately reflect your understanding of the terms and conditions of this engagement, sign and return a copy of this letter to the attention of Jennifer Kwon at the address set forth above or by electronic mail to jennifer.kwon@calderwoodharkness.com. We are delighted to have the opportunity to represent Pinnacle and the Company in connection with the IPO, and we very much look forward to working with you and your team on this Transaction.

Very truly yours,

CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law**
