Catherine E. Loomis, Esq. General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600 Wilmington, Delaware 19803

> **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Formation of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP and Related Vehicles** **Matter Number: 1003-00002**

Dear Ms. Loomis:

We are delighted to set forth the terms pursuant to which Calderwood & Harkness LLP (the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" \"us,\" or \"our\") will represent Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (\"HCP\" or the \"Client\") in connection with the formation and fundraise of the Client\'s fifth flagship private equity fund, as described in greater detail below. This letter (this \"Engagement Letter\"), when countersigned by the Client, shall constitute the binding agreement between the Firm and the Client with respect to the engagement described herein.

**[1. Engagement and Client Identification]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with the formation, structuring, and fundraise of the Client\'s fifth flagship private equity fund and the related fund vehicles described in Section 2 below (collectively, the \"Engagement\"). HCP will serve as the Sponsor and promoter of the fund and its related vehicles, and in that capacity is responsible for all aspects of the fundraise, investor relations, and fund management.

We note that HCP is a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC File No. 801-79223; CRD No. 298417) and is subject to the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

For purposes of this Engagement, HCP is the sole client of the Firm. Although we will be forming and advising on various related entities in the course of the Engagement --- including the fund partnership entities, the general partner entity, the blocker corporation, and the offshore feeder vehicle, each as identified in Section 2 below --- HCP is the sole entity to which we owe a duty of loyalty and professional responsibility. We do not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any limited partner, prospective limited partner, placement agent, lender, fund administrator, or any other third party in connection with this matter. Each such third party should engage its own legal counsel as it deems appropriate.

**[2. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The scope of our Engagement encompasses the following workstreams, each as more fully described below. Matters that fall outside the scope of this Section 2 are excluded from the Engagement unless separately agreed in writing.

**2.1 Fund Vehicles to Be Formed**

We will form and structure the following entities in connection with the fundraise (collectively, the \"Fund Complex\"):

**(a) Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP (\"HPE Fund V\" or the \"Fund\")** --- a Delaware limited partnership that will serve as the main fund vehicle for the fifth flagship private equity fund. The target hard cap for capital commitments to HPE Fund V is Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000).

**(b) Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC (the \"General Partner\")** --- a Delaware limited liability company to be organized as the sole general partner of HPE Fund V and the Parallel Fund. The sole member of the General Partner shall be HCP.

**(c) Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP (the \"Parallel Fund\")** --- a Delaware limited partnership to be organized as a parallel vehicle for the investment by certain tax-exempt and non-U.S. limited partners that may require alternative structuring to address specific tax, regulatory, or policy considerations. The Parallel Fund will invest on a substantially pari passu basis alongside the Fund.

**(d) Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP (the \"Offshore Feeder\")** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be organized as a feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors seeking to invest through a non-U.S. jurisdiction. Subject to the exclusion described in Section 2.10 below, our work with respect to the Offshore Feeder will be limited to the drafting of the exempted limited partnership agreement under New York law governing provisions, with Cayman Islands formation filings and CIMA registration to be handled by local Cayman counsel engaged by the Client.

**(e) HGF V blocker Corp. (the \"Blocker\")** --- a Delaware C corporation to be organized as a blocker entity through which certain tax-exempt investors may invest in the Fund Complex in order to mitigate exposure to unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\").

**2.2 Core Formation Work**

In connection with the formation of the Fund Complex, we will perform the following work:

> \(a\) Drafting and negotiating the Agreement of Limited Partnership of HPE Fund V LP (the \"LPA\"), which shall set forth the terms and conditions governing the formation, governance, investment activities, capital contributions, distributions, allocations, management fees, carried interest, expenses, reporting obligations, and dissolution of the Fund.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Parallel Fund, which shall contain terms and conditions substantially consistent with the LPA, adapted as necessary to accommodate the particular tax, regulatory, and structural considerations applicable to the Parallel Fund\'s investor base.
>
> \(c\) Drafting the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement of the Offshore Feeder, which shall contain terms and conditions consistent with the LPA, adapted as necessary for the Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership structure and the particular requirements of non-U.S. investors.
>
> \(d\) Drafting the Limited Liability Company Agreement of the General Partner, which shall set forth the governance, capitalization, and operating terms of the General Partner entity.
>
> \(e\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Limited Partnership for HPE Fund V LP with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(f\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Formation for Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(g\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Incorporation for HGF V blocker Corp. with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(h\) Drafting the Bylaws of HGF V blocker Corp., including provisions governing the board of directors, officers, indemnification, and corporate procedures.

**2.3 Offering Documents**

We will prepare the following offering and subscription documents for the Fund Complex:

> \(a\) Drafting and negotiating the Confidential Private Placement Memorandum (the \"PPM\") for HPE Fund V LP, which shall describe the investment strategy, key fund terms, risk factors, tax considerations, regulatory disclosures, track record information for predecessor funds (HPE Fund I through HPE Fund IV), biographies of key investment professionals, and other material information required in connection with the private placement offering.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the form Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire for each vehicle in the Fund Complex (i.e., the Main Fund, the Parallel Fund, and the Offshore Feeder), which shall include customary investor representations, warranties, and certifications (including accredited investor, qualified purchaser, ERISA, FATCA, and anti-money laundering certifications).
>
> \(c\) Drafting the Investor Suitability Questionnaire / Know Your Customer (\"KYC\") Form, incorporating current anti-money laundering and sanctions screening requirements applicable to the Fund Complex.

**2.4 Side Letters and LP Negotiations**

We will perform the following work in connection with side letter negotiations with prospective limited partners:

> \(a\) Preparing a form Side Letter template containing standard concession provisions commonly requested by institutional limited partners, including without limitation provisions addressing most favored nation (\"MFN\") rights, enhanced reporting and transparency requirements, co-investment allocation rights, transfer and secondary sale provisions, ERISA-related representations and covenants, and tax-related provisions (including withholding and allocation matters).
>
> \(b\) Negotiating individual side letters with anchor and institutional limited partners and their respective counsel. As of the date hereof, the following investors and their counsel have been identified as likely participants in the side letter negotiation process:
>
> \(i\) Northmoor State Pension System (counsel: Aldworth & McBride LLP);
>
> \(ii\) The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund (counsel: Pelham Chambers LLP);
>
> \(iii\) Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd.;
>
> \(iv\) Velthorn Family Office LLC;
>
> \(v\) Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority (counsel: Ramsden Clarke International LLP); and
>
> \(vi\) Stonewall Partners Fund of Funds III LP.
>
> Additional investors and their counsel will be identified as the fundraise progresses, and we will negotiate side letters with such investors as directed by the Client.
>
> \(c\) Preparing the form MFN Election Notice to be distributed to all limited partners entitled to elect the benefit of MFN-protected side letter provisions following each closing.

**Please note:** All work described in this Section 2.4, including the negotiation of individual side letters with limited partners and their respective counsel, will be billed on an hourly basis at the rates set forth in Section 5.1 below and is **outside** the Fee Cap described in Section 5.2 below. This carve-out reflects the inherently unpredictable nature of side letter negotiations, which are driven by the number of investors, the complexity of their requests, and the responsiveness of their counsel. Estimates of anticipated side letter negotiation costs will be provided to the Client as specific LP negotiations commence.

**2.5 Tax Structuring**

Our tax practice will advise on the following matters in connection with the formation and structuring of the Fund Complex:

> \(a\) Advising on the partnership tax classification of the Main Fund and the Parallel Fund under Subchapter K of the Code (Sections 701--777), including confirmation of classification as partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes and analysis of relevant elections.
>
> \(b\) Analyzing UBTI considerations for tax-exempt limited partners (including charitable organizations, pension plans, university endowments, and other exempt entities) and advising on the role and structure of the blocker entity in mitigating UBTI exposure under Sections 511--514 of the Code.
>
> \(c\) Analyzing effectively connected income (\"ECI\") and Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act (\"FIRPTA\") withholding issues for non-U.S. investors investing through the Offshore Feeder and/or the Main Fund, including analysis of Sections 1445 and 1446 of the Code and applicable income tax treaty provisions.
>
> \(d\) Advising on compliance with Section 1061 of the Code, including the application of the three-year holding period requirement for carried interest (applicable profits interest) received by HCP and its investment professionals in connection with the Fund Complex.
>
> \(e\) Analyzing the Cayman Islands tax neutrality of the Offshore Feeder, including consideration of the economic substance requirements under Cayman Islands law and the absence of Cayman Islands income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax applicable to the Offshore Feeder and its partners.
>
> \(f\) Preparing written tax structuring memoranda for the Client summarizing the foregoing analyses and providing recommendations regarding the optimal tax structure for the Fund Complex.
>
> \(g\) Preparing the ERISA Analysis Memorandum, which shall analyze the benefit plan investor percentage threshold under 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101(f) (as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA) and advise on procedures and monitoring mechanisms to ensure that the assets of the Fund are not treated as \"plan assets\" under ERISA --- i.e., that benefit plan investors hold less than 25% of the value of each class of equity interests in the Fund (excluding interests held by the General Partner and its affiliates).

**2.6 Regulatory and Compliance**

We will advise on the following regulatory and compliance matters:

> \(a\) Preparing and filing Form D (Notice of Exempt Offering of Securities) with the SEC within fifteen (15) days of the First Close of the Fund, in accordance with the requirements of Regulation D under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"), Rule 506(b).
>
> \(b\) Coordinating state blue sky notice filings in all U.S. states and territories where limited partners are domiciled, as required by applicable state securities laws. The number and timing of such filings will depend on the geographic distribution of the Fund\'s investor base, and filing fees incurred in connection therewith will be billed to the Client at cost.
>
> \(c\) Advising on the qualification of the Fund under Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the \"Investment Company Act\"), including confirmation that all investors in the Fund are \"qualified purchasers\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act.
>
> \(d\) Advising on Investment Advisers Act compliance matters as applicable to the fundraise, including consideration of advertising and performance presentation requirements, Form ADV disclosure updates, and custody rule compliance.
>
> \(e\) Preparing the Placement Agent Disclosure & Compliance Memorandum regarding Osprey Capital Markets LLC, which has been engaged by the Client as the placement agent for the Fund. This memorandum will address compliance with SEC guidance on placement agent disclosures, state pay-to-play restrictions, and Rule 206(4)-5 under the Investment Advisers Act (political contributions and placement agent regulations for government entity investors).

**2.7 Ancillary and Administrative Documents**

We will prepare the following ancillary and administrative documents for use in connection with the Fund\'s operations:

> \(a\) Drafting the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") Charter / Terms of Reference, setting forth the composition, authority, meeting procedures, and conflict-of-interest review protocols for the LPAC.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the form Capital Call Notice, to be used by the General Partner in connection with drawdowns of capital commitments from limited partners.
>
> \(c\) Drafting the form Distribution Notice, to be used by the General Partner in connection with distributions to limited partners.
>
> \(d\) Drafting the form Transfer (Assignment) Agreement, to be used in connection with any permitted transfer or assignment of a limited partner\'s interest in the Fund in accordance with the transfer provisions of the LPA.
>
> \(e\) Preparing the First Close Checklist, which shall set forth all conditions precedent, deliverables, filings, and corporate actions required to be completed or delivered on or prior to the First Close of the Fund.

**2.8 Legal Opinions**

We will deliver the following legal opinions at the First Close of the Fund:

> \(a\) A legal opinion addressed to the Fund, the General Partner, and (to the extent required by the LPA or any side letter) the limited partners, as to the valid formation of HPE Fund V LP and Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act and the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, respectively, and as to the enforceability of the LPA against the parties thereto (subject to customary exceptions, qualifications, and assumptions).
>
> \(b\) A legal opinion addressed to the Fund and the General Partner as to the availability of the Regulation D, Rule 506(b) exemption from registration under the Securities Act with respect to the offering and sale of limited partnership interests in the Fund, and as to the availability of the Section 3(c)(7) exclusion from registration under the Investment Company Act (subject to customary exceptions, qualifications, and assumptions, including reliance on the representations of the limited partners in their respective Subscription Agreements).

**2.9 Third-Party Agreement Review**

We will review and comment on the following third-party agreements:

> \(a\) Reviewing and marking up the Fund Administration Agreement to be entered into between the Fund and Pinnacle Fund Services LLC, the Client\'s selected fund administrator. Our review will focus on the scope of services, standard of care, liability and indemnification provisions, data security obligations, and termination provisions.
>
> \(b\) Reviewing the indicative term sheet for the subscription credit facility (the \"Credit Facility\") to be provided by Ashford National Bank, N.A. to the Fund. The Credit Facility contemplates a revolving credit commitment of up to Five Hundred Million Dollars (\$500,000,000), secured by the unfunded capital commitments of the limited partners. We will prepare a Term Sheet Review Memorandum summarizing the key terms, conditions, and legal issues raised by the indicative term sheet, including borrowing conditions, advance rates, collateral coverage ratios, events of default, and limited partner consent requirements.

**Please note:** The negotiation of definitive subscription credit facility documentation (including the credit agreement, security agreement, account control agreements, and related documents) is not included within the scope of this Engagement. If the Client desires the Firm\'s assistance in negotiating definitive Credit Facility documentation, such work will be scoped as a separate workstream and will be subject to a separate fee arrangement to be agreed upon between the parties.

**2.10 Excluded Matters**

The following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this Engagement:

> \(a\) Representation of any limited partner or prospective limited partner in the Fund Complex in connection with their investment in the Fund, the negotiation of side letters, or any other matter.
>
> \(b\) Cayman Islands legal advice. The Client shall engage local Cayman Islands counsel for the formation and filing of the Offshore Feeder with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships, and for any registration or notification requirements under the Mutual Funds Act (as revised) with the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (\"CIMA\"). We will coordinate with such Cayman Islands counsel as necessary in connection with the Engagement but will not render opinions or advice on matters of Cayman Islands law.
>
> \(c\) Negotiation of definitive subscription credit facility documentation (including the credit agreement, security documents, and ancillary financing documents), unless separately agreed in writing as described in Section 2.9 above.
>
> \(d\) Portfolio company-level acquisition work, including due diligence, negotiation and drafting of acquisition agreements, and post-closing integration matters.
>
> \(e\) Regulatory examinations or enforcement matters, including SEC examinations, inquiries, or proceedings.
>
> \(f\) Litigation of any kind, including disputes with limited partners, counterparties, portfolio companies, or regulators.

**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys will serve as the core engagement team for this matter. The Client may direct questions or communications to any member of the team, and the Responsible Partner and Billing Partner identified below will have overall supervisory responsibility for the quality and timeliness of our work product.

**Graham Sutherland** --- *Responsible Partner*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (Wilmington office). Mr. Sutherland has twenty-four (24) years of experience in private equity fund formation and investment management matters. He will have overall responsibility for the Engagement and will serve as the primary relationship partner for HCP. Mr. Sutherland can be reached at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com or (302) 555-7810.

**Pamela Cross** --- *Billing Partner*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (New York office). Ms. Cross has twenty (20) years of experience in fund formation and institutional investor relations. She will oversee billing, budgeting, and day-to-day project management for the Engagement, including coordination of internal resources and monitoring of progress against the fundraise timeline. Ms. Cross can be reached at pcross@calderwoodharkness.com or (212) 555-9415.

**Stephen Adler** --- *Lead Associate*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (Wilmington office). Mr. Adler is a seventh-year associate with significant experience in the formation of private equity, venture capital, and credit fund vehicles. He will serve as the primary drafter of the LPA, PPM, subscription documents, and ancillary formation documents for the Fund Complex. Mr. Adler can be reached at sadler@calderwoodharkness.com or (302) 555-7822.

**Theresa Kim** --- *Working Associate*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (New York office). Ms. Kim is a fourth-year associate who will assist with document drafting, third-party agreement review (including the Pinnacle Fund Services administration agreement and the Ashford National Bank term sheet review), regulatory filings (Form D, blue sky notices), and investor communications. Ms. Kim can be reached at tkim@calderwoodharkness.com or (212) 555-9428.

**Sylvia Hartwell** --- *Specialist Partner*, Tax Practice Group (New York office). Ms. Hartwell has eighteen (18) years of experience in partnership taxation, fund structuring, and international tax planning for private investment funds. She will advise on all fund-level tax structuring matters described in Section 2.5 above, including the design of the blocker entity, the structure of the parallel vehicles, the ERISA analysis, Section 1061 carried interest compliance, and international tax considerations for the Offshore Feeder and non-U.S. investors. Ms. Hartwell can be reached at shartwell@calderwoodharkness.com or (212) 555-9440.

Additional attorneys, paraprofessionals, or other support staff may be assigned to the Engagement as needed to ensure timely and efficient delivery of work product. The Client will be informed of any material changes to the composition of the core engagement team.

**[4. Client Responsibilities]{.underline}**

The efficient and timely completion of the Engagement will depend on the Client\'s cooperation in providing information, reviewing drafts, and coordinating with third parties. In particular, the Client agrees to the following:

> \(a\) **Information Provision.** The Client shall provide, on a timely basis, all information necessary for the preparation of the formation and offering documents, including (without limitation) information regarding the investment strategy, target geographies and sectors, fund terms (including management fees, carried interest, hurdle rate, waterfall structure, GP commitment, key person provisions, and investment period terms), and track record data for the predecessor funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP), including realized and unrealized performance data, attribution, and relevant disclaimers.
>
> \(b\) **Draft Review Timeline.** The Client shall review and provide comments on drafts within the timelines agreed upon between the Client and the Firm in order to meet the following target fundraise schedule:
>
> \(i\) PPM initial draft delivered by the Firm to the Client: **May 1, 2025**;
>
> \(ii\) LPA initial draft delivered by the Firm to the Client: **May 9, 2025**;
>
> \(iii\) Distribution of PPM, LPA summary, and subscription documents to prospective limited partners: **June 2, 2025**; and
>
> \(iv\) Target First Close: **August 15, 2025**.
>
> The foregoing timeline is subject to adjustment based on the Client\'s review and comment cycle and the progress of investor negotiations. The Firm and the Client will communicate regularly regarding the status of the fundraise timeline and will work cooperatively to address any delays or changes in schedule.
>
> \(c\) **Investor Counsel Coordination.** The Client shall coordinate communications with investor-side counsel, including but not limited to:
>
> \(i\) Aldworth & McBride LLP, counsel for Northmoor State Pension System;
>
> \(ii\) Pelham Chambers LLP, counsel for The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund; and
>
> \(iii\) Ramsden Clarke International LLP, counsel for Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority.
>
> The Client shall provide introductions and facilitate initial communications between the Firm and investor-side counsel as necessary to commence side letter negotiations.
>
> \(d\) **Third-Party Coordination.** The Client shall be responsible for the engagement and coordination of the placement agent (Osprey Capital Markets LLC) and the fund administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC), and shall facilitate the Firm\'s access to such parties and their respective documentation as necessary for the Firm to perform the work described in Section 2.
>
> \(e\) **Cayman Islands Counsel.** The Client shall engage local Cayman Islands counsel as necessary for the formation and regulatory filings of the Offshore Feeder. The Client shall provide the Firm with the identity and contact information of such Cayman Islands counsel in a timely manner so that we may coordinate the drafting of the Offshore Feeder\'s exempted limited partnership agreement.
>
> \(f\) **PPM Data.** The Client shall provide final data for the predecessor fund performance tables, team biographies, and other factual content to be included in the PPM. The Client shall be responsible for the accuracy and completeness of all factual information provided for inclusion in the PPM.

**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**

**5.1 Billing Rates**

Our current standard hourly billing rates for calendar year 2025 are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper Level**                **Rate Range**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Partners                            \$1,450 -- \$1,650 per hour

  Associates                          \$850 -- \$1,050 per hour
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The specific billing rate for each attorney will be determined based on the attorney\'s seniority, expertise, and role on the Engagement. Within the above ranges, current hourly rates for the core engagement team members are: Mr. Sutherland (\$1,625/hr); Ms. Cross (\$1,575/hr); Ms. Hartwell (\$1,600/hr); Mr. Adler (\$1,025/hr); and Ms. Kim (\$900/hr).

Billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective as of January 1 of each calendar year. The Client will be notified in advance of any rate changes applicable to the Engagement. Any such rate change will apply only to time recorded on or after the effective date of the change.

Paraprofessional and support staff time, if any, will be billed at the Firm\'s standard rates for such personnel, which currently range from \$350 to \$550 per hour depending on the paraprofessional\'s experience and role.

**5.2 Fee Cap --- Core Formation Work**

The aggregate professional fees for the core fund formation work described in Sections 2.1 through 2.3 and Sections 2.5 through 2.10 of this Engagement Letter shall not exceed **Two Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,200,000)** (the \"Fee Cap\"). The Fee Cap covers all professional time of the engagement team members for the enumerated core workstreams, regardless of the number of hours actually expended by the team.

Based on our experience with comparable fund formations and our preliminary assessment of the complexity of the Fund Complex, we estimate that the actual professional fees for the core formation workstreams will fall within a range of approximately \$1,800,000 to \$2,200,000, depending on the complexity and number of vehicles ultimately formed, the scope and complexity of regulatory filings, and the extent of legal opinion work required. We will endeavor to manage the Engagement efficiently and to keep costs at the lower end of this range to the extent practicable.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Fee Cap applies exclusively to the core workstreams enumerated above and does not apply to the side letter negotiation work described in Section 2.4, which is billed hourly as set forth in Section 5.3 below.

**5.3 Side Letter Negotiation --- Hourly**

All work described in Section 2.4 of this Engagement Letter (side letter template preparation, negotiation of individual side letters with limited partners and their respective counsel, and preparation of MFN election notices) shall be billed on an hourly basis at the rates set forth in Section 5.1 above and is **not** subject to the Fee Cap. The total cost of side letter negotiation work is inherently dependent on the number of limited partners seeking side letter accommodations, the nature and complexity of the concessions requested, and the responsiveness and negotiation posture of investor-side counsel.

We will provide the Client with periodic estimates of anticipated side letter negotiation costs as specific LP negotiations commence, and we will consult with the Client regarding scope and budget as the negotiation process progresses. We anticipate providing an initial estimate of aggregate side letter negotiation costs upon identification of the initial group of anchor investors and their counsel.

**5.4 Expenses.** Reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred in connection with the Engagement will be billed to the Client at cost, without markup. Such disbursements may include, without limitation, the following:

> \(a\) Delaware Secretary of State filing fees for certificates of limited partnership, certificates of formation, and certificates of incorporation;
>
> \(b\) SEC Form D filing fees;
>
> \(c\) State blue sky notice filing fees;
>
> \(d\) Travel expenses (airfare, lodging, ground transportation, and meals) incurred in connection with meetings, closings, and investor counsel negotiations that require in-person attendance;
>
> \(e\) Overnight delivery and courier charges;
>
> \(f\) Third-party document reproduction and printing costs; and
>
> \(g\) Other reasonable and customary out-of-pocket costs directly related to the Engagement.

We will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring expenses and will seek the Client\'s approval for any single expense item exceeding \$5,000.

**5.5 Billing and Payment**

Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered on a monthly basis, in arrears, reflecting time and expenses incurred during the preceding calendar month. Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed description of the services performed, the timekeeper(s) responsible, and the hours recorded by each timekeeper.

Payment of each invoice is due within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Invoices that remain unpaid beyond thirty (30) days may be subject to a late payment charge at the rate of 1.0% per month on the outstanding balance, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

All invoices shall be directed to:

> Jonathan P. Birch Partner, Head of Operations & Chief Financial Officer Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600 Wilmington, Delaware 19803
>
> Email: jbirch@harrowgatecapital.com

The Client may request additional invoice copies be sent to other designated personnel, and the Firm will accommodate such requests.

**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

All information provided by the Client to the Firm in connection with the Engagement, including but not limited to fund terms, investment strategy, track record data, investor identities, business plans, financial projections, and proprietary methodologies, shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed by the Firm to any third party except:

> \(a\) as authorized by the Client, whether in writing or by reasonable implication from the nature of the Engagement (for example, disclosure of information to prospective limited partners through the PPM, or to the SEC through Form D filings);
>
> \(b\) as required by law, regulation, court order, or the rules of professional conduct governing the Firm\'s attorneys; or
>
> \(c\) as necessary in the course of performing the Engagement, including but not limited to filing documents with the Delaware Secretary of State, the SEC, or state securities regulators, or communicating with investor-side counsel in connection with side letter negotiations (with the Client\'s knowledge and direction).

The Firm maintains and enforces standard information security protocols, including secure document management systems, encrypted email communications, restricted access to client files, and periodic cybersecurity training for all Firm personnel. The Firm\'s information security practices are designed to comply with applicable data protection laws and professional responsibility requirements.

**[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Client files, documents, and work product generated in connection with the Engagement will be retained by the Firm in accordance with Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s document retention policy, a copy of which is available upon request. Under the Firm\'s current policy, client files are retained for a minimum period of seven (7) years following the conclusion or termination of the Engagement, after which time the Firm may destroy such files in accordance with the policy, upon reasonable prior notice to the Client.

The Client may request the return of original documents at any time during or after the Engagement. Upon receipt of such a request, the Firm will return original documents within a commercially reasonable time. The Firm may retain copies of all documents for its own files, subject to the confidentiality obligations set forth in Section 6 above.

**[8. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP has conducted a conflicts check as of the date hereof, consistent with the Firm\'s standard conflicts clearance procedures, and has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude the Firm from undertaking this Engagement.

The Client acknowledges that Calderwood & Harkness LLP is a large, multi-practice law firm that represents numerous private equity sponsors, institutional investors, placement agents, fund administrators, lenders, and other participants in the investment management industry in a range unrelated matters. The Client agrees that such representations of other parties in unrelated matters do not constitute a conflict of interest with respect to this Engagement and do not preclude the Firm from undertaking or continuing such representations.

In the event that an actual or potential conflict of interest arises during the course of the Engagement --- whether as a result of a new representation, a change in circumstances, or otherwise --- Calderwood & Harkness LLP will promptly notify the Client and will take appropriate steps to address the conflict, which may include seeking an informed written waiver from the Client and/or the other affected party or parties, or, if such a waiver cannot be obtained, withdrawing from the affected representation in accordance with applicable rules of professional conduct.

**[9. Limitation of Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement is limited to the matters described in Section 2 of this Engagement Letter. Calderwood & Harkness LLP does not undertake to represent the Client in any matter beyond the scope described herein unless separately agreed in writing between the Firm and the Client. Any expansion of the scope of this Engagement, including the addition of new workstreams, the formation of additional fund vehicles, or the undertaking of portfolio company-level work, shall require a written supplement or amendment to this Engagement Letter or a separate engagement letter, as appropriate.

The Firm\'s engagement is with HCP as an entity. The Firm does not represent any individual partner, member, officer, director, or employee of HCP in their personal capacity, nor does the Firm represent any limited partner or prospective limited partner of the Fund or any other vehicle within the Fund Complex. Each such individual or entity should engage its own independent legal counsel to the extent it requires legal advice in connection with the Fund or any related matter.

**[10. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter and the relationship between Calderwood & Harkness LLP and the Client, including any disputes arising out of or relating to this Engagement Letter or the Engagement, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

**[11. Termination]{.underline}**

Either the Firm or the Client may terminate this Engagement upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other party. Such notice may be delivered by email or by first-class mail to the addresses set forth herein (or such other address as either party may designate in writing from time to time).

Upon termination of the Engagement for any reason, the Client shall remain obligated to pay all professional fees and out-of-pocket expenses incurred by the Firm through the effective date of termination, including any fees and expenses billed but unpaid as of such date. The Firm shall render a final invoice within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination.

Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness LLP shall cooperate with the Client in effecting an orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client, including the prompt delivery of work product, files, and documents to such successor counsel, subject to the Client\'s satisfaction of all outstanding fee and expense obligations. The Firm\'s obligations under Sections 6 (Confidentiality) and 7 (Document Retention) shall survive termination of the Engagement.

**[12. Acceptance]{.underline}**

If the terms set forth in this Engagement Letter are acceptable to the Client, please indicate your agreement by executing and returning a copy of this letter to the undersigned at the address set forth below (or by email to gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com). This Engagement Letter, when countersigned by the Client, shall constitute the binding agreement between Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC with respect to the Engagement described herein, superseding any prior oral or written communications between the parties regarding the same subject matter.

We are grateful for the opportunity to work with Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC on this important transaction and look forward to a productive and successful engagement.

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law**

425 Park Avenue, 31st Floor New York, NY 10022 Tel: (212) 554-7000

Fax: (212) 554-7001

www.calderwoodharkness.com

May 19, 2025

**VIA EMAIL AND OVERNIGHT DELIVERY**

Derek Wainwright, Esq. General Counsel Vantage Mobility Systems Corp. 4100 Industrial Parkway Auburn Hills, MI 48326

Dear Mr. Wainwright:

We are writing to confirm the terms of the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") by Vantage Mobility Systems Corp., a Delaware corporation (\"VMS\" or the \"Company\"), and to set forth the scope of our representation, the fee arrangements, and other terms and conditions governing our relationship. We ask that you review this engagement letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, execute and return a copy to us at your earliest convenience.

**[1. Engagement and Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by VMS in connection with the documentation and closing of a \$45,000,000 Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility (the \"Facility\"). The Facility is to be arranged by Pinnacle National Bank, N.A. (\"Pinnacle\"), acting as Sole Lead Arranger, Sole Bookrunner, Administrative Agent, Collateral Agent, Issuing Lender, and Swing Line Lender, with a three-lender syndicate consisting of Pinnacle, Great Lakes Commercial Lending Corp., and Ironbridge Capital Finance, LLC (collectively, the \"Lenders\"). The Firm will serve as borrower\'s counsel to VMS in connection with the Facility.

The purpose of the Facility, as described in the commitment letter executed on May 16, 2025, is to finance tooling capital expenditures associated with new and replacement program launches for VMS\'s original equipment manufacturer (\"OEM\") customer base. In addition, the Facility will be available for general corporate purposes, subject to a twenty-five percent (25%) sublimit on borrowings applied to general corporate use. We understand that VMS is a portfolio company of Ridgecrest Capital Partners, LP (\"Ridgecrest\" or the \"Sponsor\"), and that Ridgecrest Automotive Holdings, LLC serves as the direct parent and holding company of VMS.

The scope of work to be performed by the Firm under this engagement specifically includes the following:

> \(a\) **Credit Agreement.** Drafting and negotiating the Credit Agreement, including all schedules, exhibits, and annexes thereto, reflecting the terms set forth in the commitment letter and the related term sheet, and all ancillary loan documents contemplated thereby, including promissory notes, borrowing notices, compliance certificates, and other operational documents required under the Facility.
>
> \(b\) **Guarantee and Collateral Agreement.** Drafting the Guarantee and Collateral Agreement to be entered into by VMS and any subsidiary guarantors in favor of Pinnacle as Collateral Agent for the benefit of the Lenders, providing for a first-priority security interest in substantially all assets of VMS and the guarantors, including accounts receivable, inventory, equipment, general intangibles, intellectual property, and other personal property.
>
> \(c\) **Intercreditor Agreement.** Reviewing and negotiating the Intercreditor Agreement, which will be an equal-priority intercreditor agreement between the Facility and the existing first-lien term loan outstanding under the Existing Credit Agreement dated March 15, 2022, among VMS, Pinnacle (as administrative agent), and the lenders party thereto (the \"Existing Credit Agreement\"). The Intercreditor Agreement will allocate rights and priorities between the two first-lien facilities and govern enforcement rights, standstill provisions, and proceeds-sharing arrangements.
>
> \(d\) **Sponsor Limited Guarantee.** Reviewing and commenting on the Sponsor Limited Guarantee to be provided by Ridgecrest Automotive Holdings, LLC in favor of Pinnacle as Administrative Agent, which guarantee is expected to be capped at \$5,000,000 and limited to certain specified obligations under the Credit Agreement.
>
> \(e\) **UCC-1 Financing Statements.** Preparing UCC-1 financing statements for filing with the Delaware Secretary of State (as the jurisdiction of organization of VMS) and the Michigan Department of State (as the jurisdiction where certain collateral may be located or where filing may be required), and conducting appropriate lien searches in connection therewith.
>
> \(f\) **IP Security Agreements.** Preparing intellectual property security agreements (covering patents, trademarks, and any other registrable intellectual property of VMS) for filing with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (\"USPTO\"), as necessary to perfect the Lenders\' security interest in such intellectual property.
>
> \(g\) **Deposit Account Control Agreements.** Reviewing and advising on deposit account control agreements (\"DACAs\") to be entered into among VMS, the applicable depository bank (Lakeshore Trust Company), and Pinnacle as Collateral Agent, in order to provide the Lenders with control over deposit accounts maintained by VMS at Lakeshore Trust Company.
>
> \(h\) **Closing Deliverables.** Preparing closing deliverables, including the Secretary\'s Certificate (attaching certified copies of VMS\'s certificate of incorporation, bylaws, and board resolutions authorizing the Facility), the Officer\'s Closing Certificate (certifying the accuracy of representations and warranties and the absence of defaults as of the closing date), and the Funds Flow Memorandum detailing the disbursement of loan proceeds on the closing date.
>
> \(i\) **Legal Opinion.** Delivering the Borrower\'s Counsel legal opinion at closing, which opinion will cover corporate authorization of VMS to enter into the Facility documentation, enforceability of the loan documents under the laws of the State of New York, no-conflicts with VMS\'s organizational documents and applicable law, and UCC perfection of the security interests granted under the Guarantee and Collateral Agreement.
>
> \(j\) **Closing Checklist.** Preparing and maintaining a comprehensive Closing Checklist identifying all documents, certificates, filings, and other deliverables required in connection with the closing of the Facility, and updating the Closing Checklist as the transaction progresses.
>
> \(k\) **Coordination with Lenders\' Counsel.** Coordinating with Hargrove, Stein & Calloway LLP, counsel to Pinnacle and the Lender syndicate, on the negotiation and finalization of the Facility documentation, the resolution of open issues, and the logistics of closing.

The Facility is governed by, and all documentation in connection therewith will be prepared under, the laws of the State of New York. The targeted closing date for the Facility is June 30, 2025, and the Firm will use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver its work product in a manner consistent with that timeline, subject to the cooperation of VMS, the Lenders, and their respective counsel.

**[2. Scope Limitations and Exclusions]{.underline}**

The engagement described in Section 1 is limited to the documentation and closing of the Facility. Our representation does not extend to, and VMS should not rely upon the Firm for advice in connection with, the following matters, which are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:

> \(a\) **Regulatory Matters.** Regulatory advice regarding the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (\"OCC\"), the Federal Reserve, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, or any other banking or financial regulatory authority, including any regulatory approvals or compliance obligations of the Lenders.
>
> \(b\) **Tax Advice.** Tax advice of any nature, including federal, state, local, or foreign income tax, franchise tax, sales and use tax, transfer tax, or withholding tax matters. VMS should consult with its own tax advisors regarding the tax implications of the Facility and the transactions contemplated thereby.
>
> \(c\) **Existing Credit Agreement.** Any advice relating to the Existing Credit Agreement dated March 15, 2022, including the interpretation, enforcement, amendment, or waiver of any provision thereof, except as is strictly necessary for the purpose of coordinating the Intercreditor Agreement with the terms and conditions of the Existing Credit Agreement.
>
> \(d\) **Environmental, Employment, Real Property, and ERISA Matters.** Advice concerning environmental law and compliance, employment and labor matters, real property title, survey, zoning, or environmental site assessments, or matters arising under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or related pension or benefit plan matters.
>
> \(e\) **Post-Closing Matters.** Any future amendments, restatements, supplements, waivers, consents, forbearances, or workouts under the Facility following the closing date, unless the Firm is separately engaged in writing to perform such services.
>
> \(f\) **Litigation and Disputes.** Representation in any litigation, arbitration, mediation, or other dispute resolution proceeding arising from or related to the Facility, the Credit Agreement, or any of the ancillary loan documents.

We wish to make clear that the Firm represents only VMS in its capacity as borrower under the Facility. The Firm does not represent, and this engagement does not create an attorney-client relationship with, Ridgecrest Capital Partners, LP, Ridgecrest Automotive Holdings, LLC, any subsidiary or affiliate of VMS, or any officer, director, employee, or equityholder of VMS in their individual capacities. If any such entity or person requires separate legal counsel in connection with the Facility or any related matter, we recommend that they engage independent counsel.

**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The Firm has assembled the following team to handle this engagement:

> **Responsible Partner:** Claudia Merritt, Partner, Banking & Finance Practice Group. Ms. Merritt will have overall responsibility for the engagement, including the client relationship, strategic direction, and quality of all work product delivered to VMS. Ms. Merritt will participate in key negotiations and will review all principal documents prior to delivery.
>
> **Billing Partner:** Ian Blackwood, Partner, Banking & Finance Practice Group. Mr. Blackwood will be responsible for billing, fee arrangements, and the financial administration of the engagement, including the preparation and review of invoices and the monitoring of fees against the Fee Cap described in Section 4 below.
>
> **Lead Associate:** Marcus Leung, Banking & Finance Practice Group. Mr. Leung will be responsible for the day-to-day management of the engagement, including the drafting of documents, the coordination of negotiations with Hargrove, Stein & Calloway LLP, the management of due diligence, and the preparation of closing deliverables.
>
> **Working Associate:** Sophie Tremblay, Banking & Finance Practice Group. Ms. Tremblay will support the engagement by assisting with drafting, managing the Closing Checklist, preparing ancillary documents (including UCC-1 financing statements, IP security agreements, and the Secretary\'s Certificate), and coordinating filings.

Additional attorneys, paralegals, or other support staff may be assigned to the engagement as needed to ensure timely and efficient completion of the work. VMS will be informed of any material changes to the core engagement team identified above. Should VMS have any concerns about staffing, we encourage you to raise them promptly with Claudia Merritt.

For day-to-day matters, including the exchange of document drafts, scheduling of calls, and coordination of closing logistics, VMS\'s primary point of contact at the Firm will be Marcus Leung. For substantive legal questions and strategic issues relating to the Facility, VMS should contact Claudia Merritt directly.

**[4. Fees and Billing Arrangements]{.underline}**

**4.1 Hourly Rates**

The Firm\'s current standard hourly rates applicable to this engagement are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper Category**             **Hourly Rate**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Partners                            \$1,350

  Associates                          \$850

  Paralegals / Legal Assistants       \$350 -- \$450
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

Paralegal and legal assistant time, if applicable, will be billed at the Firm\'s then-current rates, which currently fall within the range of \$350 to \$450 per hour depending on the experience and seniority of the individual. The hourly rates set forth above are subject to annual adjustment in accordance with the Firm\'s standard rate-setting process; provided, however, that the rates applicable to this engagement will not be adjusted during the term of this engagement unless the engagement extends beyond December 31, 2025.

**4.2 Fee Cap**

Notwithstanding the hourly rate structure described in Section 4.1 above, the aggregate documentation fees charged by the Firm for this engagement shall not exceed One Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$185,000) (the \"Fee Cap\"). The Fee Cap represents the maximum amount that will be billed for professional services (i.e., attorney and paralegal time) in connection with the engagement.

The Fee Cap is exclusive of disbursements, expenses, and any charges described in Section 4.3 below, which will be billed separately. The Fee Cap covers all work described in Section 1, from the opening of the engagement through and including the closing of the Facility, which is currently targeted for June 30, 2025.

In the event that (i) the closing of the Facility is delayed beyond September 30, 2025, or (ii) the scope of the engagement materially changes from that described in Section 1, the Firm reserves the right to discuss an adjustment to the Fee Cap with VMS. For the avoidance of doubt, a material change in scope shall include, without limitation, additional documentation requests by the Lenders or their counsel that are not reasonably contemplated by the term sheet or commitment letter as of the date hereof, material changes to the structure of the Facility (including, for example, the addition of a term loan tranche, a change in the collateral package, or a restructuring of the guarantee arrangements), or the addition of new lenders to the syndicate beyond the current three-lender group. Any adjustment to the Fee Cap will require the prior written agreement of VMS and the Firm.

**4.3 Disbursements and Expenses**

In addition to professional fees, VMS will reimburse the Firm for reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements and expenses incurred in connection with the engagement. Reimbursable disbursements and expenses include, but are not limited to, the following:

> \(a\) Filing fees, including UCC-1 filing fees with the Delaware Secretary of State and the Michigan Department of State, USPTO filing fees for IP security agreements, and fees for good standing certificates, certified copies, and lien searches;
>
> \(b\) Online research charges, including charges for legal databases such as Westmark Data Systems and Sundial Solutions, to the extent incurred in connection with work performed for VMS;
>
> \(c\) Courier, overnight delivery (e.g., Severin Partners LLC, Halcyon Partners LLC), and postage charges;
>
> \(d\) Travel expenses, if required in connection with the engagement, including airfare (at coach class), reasonable hotel accommodations, ground transportation, and meals, in each case subject to the Firm\'s standard travel expense policy;
>
> \(e\) Photocopying and document production costs, including costs associated with the reproduction and binding of closing binders; and
>
> \(f\) Closing expenses, including notary fees and other charges directly attributable to the closing of the Facility.

Based on our experience with transactions of this nature and size, we estimate that total disbursements for this engagement will be in the range of \$5,000 to \$10,000. We will endeavor to keep disbursements to a minimum and will consult with VMS before incurring any single disbursement in excess of \$1,000 (excluding routine filing fees).

**4.4 Billing and Payment**

The Firm will render monthly invoices to VMS for professional fees and disbursements incurred during the preceding calendar month. The first invoice is expected to be rendered in June 2025, reflecting services performed during the month of May 2025 and the initial period of the engagement.

Payment of each invoice is due within thirty (30) days of the date of such invoice. Invoices will contain reasonable detail regarding the nature of services performed, the identity of the attorneys and other timekeepers performing such services, the time spent by each timekeeper, and the applicable hourly rate. Time entries will be described in sufficient detail to enable VMS to evaluate the reasonableness of the charges.

All invoices shall be sent to:

> Derek Wainwright, Esq. General Counsel Vantage Mobility Systems Corp. 4100 Industrial Parkway Auburn Hills, MI 48326

with a copy to:

> Linda S. Nakamura Chief Financial Officer Vantage Mobility Systems Corp. 4100 Industrial Parkway Auburn Hills, MI 48326

VMS may, at any time, designate an alternative delivery method for invoices, including an electronic billing portal or email address, by providing written notice to the Firm. The Firm will comply with reasonable electronic billing requirements of VMS, including submission through any third-party e-billing platform that VMS may utilize.

**4.5 Payment of Third-Party Fees**

We note for the avoidance of doubt that VMS, as borrower under the Facility, is expected to bear certain fees and expenses payable to third parties in connection with the closing of the Facility. These obligations are set forth in the commitment letter executed on May 16, 2025, and include, among other items:

> \(a\) The legal fees and disbursements of Hargrove, Stein & Calloway LLP, counsel to Pinnacle and the Lender syndicate;
>
> \(b\) The upfront fee of \$450,000 payable to the Lenders at closing;
>
> \(c\) The arrangement fee of \$125,000 payable to Pinnacle as Sole Lead Arranger at closing;
>
> \(d\) The annual administrative agent fee of \$75,000 payable to Pinnacle as Administrative Agent; and
>
> \(e\) Other closing costs, including title insurance premiums, appraisal fees, and similar charges, as set forth in the commitment letter.

These third-party fees and expenses are not included in, and are entirely separate from, the C&H Fee Cap. The Firm\'s fees under this engagement letter are independent of VMS\'s obligations to pay such third-party fees and expenses, and VMS\'s obligation to pay the Firm\'s fees is not contingent upon or affected by the status of any such third-party payments.

**[5. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

The Firm will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by VMS, its officers, directors, employees, agents, and advisors in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations under the New York Rules of Professional Conduct and applicable law. The Firm will not disclose confidential information to any third party without VMS\'s prior consent, except to the extent that disclosure is:

> \(a\) required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or subpoena;
>
> \(b\) required by professional regulatory requirements, including the rules of professional conduct governing the Firm\'s attorneys;
>
> \(c\) necessary in the ordinary course of performing services under this engagement, including, without limitation, the sharing of information with Hargrove, Stein & Calloway LLP in connection with the negotiation and documentation of the Facility, or the provision of information to filing offices (such as the Delaware Secretary of State, the Michigan Department of State, and the USPTO) in connection with UCC filings and other public filings contemplated by the engagement; or
>
> \(d\) authorized by VMS in writing.

The Firm\'s obligation of confidentiality as described in this Section 5 shall survive the termination or conclusion of this engagement and shall continue in full force and effect regardless of the reason for termination.

**[6. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

The Firm has conducted a conflicts check with respect to this engagement based on the information currently available to it, including the identities of VMS, Ridgecrest Capital Partners, LP, Ridgecrest Automotive Holdings, LLC, Pinnacle National Bank, N.A., Great Lakes Commercial Lending Corp., Ironbridge Capital Finance, LLC, and Hargrove, Stein & Calloway LLP. Based on the results of that conflicts check, the Firm is not aware of any conflict of interest that would prevent or limit its ability to represent VMS in connection with the Facility documentation.

We wish to disclose, however, that Calderwood & Harkness LLP is a large, multi-practice law firm that represents a broad range of clients across numerous industries and practice areas. The Firm may from time to time represent other clients, including financial institutions, private equity sponsors, and their respective portfolio companies and affiliates, in matters that are unrelated to this engagement. By executing this engagement letter, VMS acknowledges and consents to such representations, provided that they do not involve the Facility or any matter that is directly adverse to VMS in connection with the Facility. This consent does not extend to any representation that would involve the assertion of a claim against VMS, the defense of a claim by VMS, or the negotiation of a transaction in which the interests of another client are directly opposed to those of VMS with respect to the Facility.

If, during the course of this engagement, the Firm becomes aware of any actual or potential conflict of interest that may affect its ability to continue representing VMS, the Firm will promptly notify VMS and take appropriate steps in accordance with the applicable rules of professional conduct, which may include, depending on the circumstances, obtaining informed written consent from the affected parties, implementing an ethical screen within the Firm, or, if necessary, withdrawing from the engagement.

**[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Upon the conclusion of this engagement, whether by closing of the Facility, termination, or otherwise, the Firm will retain the engagement files (including electronic and paper files) in accordance with its document retention policies. The Firm\'s current policy provides for a minimum retention period of seven (7) years from the closing date of the Facility (or, if the engagement is terminated prior to closing, seven years from the date of termination).

Notwithstanding the foregoing, VMS should maintain its own copies of all original documents, executed agreements, closing deliverables, and other materials received from the Firm or generated in connection with the Facility. The Firm\'s retention of engagement files is for the Firm\'s own records and does not relieve VMS of the obligation to maintain its own files.

Following the expiration of the retention period, the Firm may, upon not less than sixty (60) days\' prior written notice to VMS (at VMS\'s last known address), destroy or dispose of engagement files without further obligation to VMS. If VMS requests the return of any documents or files prior to or following the expiration of the retention period, the Firm will make commercially reasonable efforts to comply with such request, and VMS shall bear any costs associated with the retrieval, copying, and delivery of such files.

**[8. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time, with or without cause, upon written notice to the other party. Termination by VMS shall be effective upon the Firm\'s receipt of written notice. Termination by the Firm shall be effective upon VMS\'s receipt of written notice, subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations to provide reasonable notice and to avoid material prejudice to VMS\'s interests.

In the event of termination, VMS shall be responsible for payment of all fees earned and disbursements incurred by the Firm through the date of termination, subject to the Fee Cap. If the engagement is terminated prior to the completion of the work described in Section 1, the Fee Cap shall be applied on a pro rata basis in proportion to the services rendered through the date of termination relative to the total scope of services contemplated by the engagement.

Upon termination, the Firm will take reasonable steps to protect VMS\'s interests, including cooperating in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel (if any), providing copies of work product and files to VMS or its successor counsel, and complying with any applicable court or regulatory requirements regarding withdrawal of counsel. VMS shall reimburse the Firm for reasonable costs incurred in connection with such transition.

**[9. Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**

To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the Firm\'s aggregate liability to VMS and its affiliates, successors, and assigns arising from or related to the services performed (or failed to be performed) under this engagement, whether based on contract, tort, negligence, strict liability, professional malpractice, or any other legal or equitable theory, shall not exceed the total amount of professional fees actually paid by VMS to the Firm under this engagement letter.

In no event shall the Firm be liable to VMS or any other person or entity for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages of any kind, including but not limited to lost profits, loss of business opportunity, diminution in value, or loss of data, arising from or related to this engagement, regardless of whether the Firm has been advised of the possibility of such damages and regardless of the form of action.

Nothing in this Section 9 shall be construed to limit or restrict the Firm\'s liability for fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence, or to limit any rights or remedies that may not be waived or limited under applicable law or the rules of professional conduct.

**[10. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**

This engagement letter and the relationship between the Firm and VMS shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflicts of law provisions that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this engagement letter, the services provided hereunder, or the breach, termination, or validity hereof, shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered in New York, New York, in accordance with the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association then in effect, before a single arbitrator mutually agreed upon by the parties (or, failing agreement, appointed in accordance with such rules). The arbitrator shall have the authority to award any remedy available under applicable law, subject to the limitations set forth in Section 9. The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding upon the parties, and judgment upon the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. Alternatively, the parties may agree in writing to resolve any such dispute through mediation or other mutually agreed-upon dispute resolution mechanism prior to or in lieu of arbitration.

Each party shall bear its own attorneys\' fees and costs in connection with any arbitration proceeding, unless the arbitrator determines that the claims or defenses of the non-prevailing party were frivolous or brought in bad faith, in which case the arbitrator may award reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs to the prevailing party.

**[11. Entire Agreement and Amendments]{.underline}**

This engagement letter, together with the Calderwood & Harkness LLP Standard Terms of Business enclosed herewith and incorporated herein by reference, constitutes the entire agreement between the Firm and VMS with respect to the subject matter hereof and sets forth the complete understanding of the parties regarding the terms and conditions of the Firm\'s engagement. This engagement letter supersedes all prior discussions, negotiations, understandings, proposals, and agreements, whether written or oral, between the Firm and VMS relating to the engagement described herein.

This engagement letter may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by an authorized representative of each of the Firm and VMS. No waiver of any provision of this engagement letter shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. The failure of either party to enforce any provision of this engagement letter shall not constitute a waiver of such party\'s right to enforce such provision or any other provision in the future.

**[12. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**

We respectfully request that VMS acknowledge and accept the terms of this engagement letter by having an authorized representative sign and return a copy to the Firm at the address set forth above, or by electronic means as described below.

This engagement letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Counterparts may be delivered by electronic means, including by Portable Document Format (PDF) transmission via email or through the DocuSign electronic signature platform, and any such electronically delivered counterpart shall have the same legal force and effect as an original ink-signed counterpart.

This engagement shall be deemed effective as of May 19, 2025, the date first written above, regardless of the date on which VMS executes and returns this letter.

We look forward to working with you and the VMS team on this matter. Please do not hesitate to contact Claudia Merritt at (212) 554-7120 or cmerritt@calderwoodharkness.com, or Marcus Leung at (212) 554-7245 or mleung@calderwoodharkness.com, with any questions regarding this engagement letter or the Facility documentation.

Very truly yours,

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Name: Claudia Merritt

Title: Partner, Banking & Finance Practice Group

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Name: Ian Blackwood

Title: Partner, Banking & Finance Practice Group

**ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND ACCEPTANCE**

The undersigned, on behalf of Vantage Mobility Systems Corp., hereby acknowledges receipt of this engagement letter, confirms that the undersigned is duly authorized to execute this engagement letter on behalf of the Company, and accepts and agrees to the terms and conditions set forth herein.

**ACKNOWLEDGED AND ACCEPTED:**

**VANTAGE MOBILITY SYSTEMS CORP.**

from pathlib import Path
from zipfile import ZipFile
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET
import re
root=Path('documents/matters')
ns={'w':'http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main'}
rows=[]
for p in sorted(root.glob('*/*/engagement*.docx')):
    try:
        with ZipFile(p) as z:
            xml=z.read('word/document.xml')
        tree=ET.fromstring(xml)
        paras=[]
        for para in tree.findall('.//w:p',ns):
            txt=''.join(t.text or '' for t in para.findall('.//w:t',ns))
            if txt.strip(): paras.append(txt.strip())
        text='\n'.join(paras)
        rows.append((p.parent.parent.name,str(p.relative_to(root)),text[:1800]))
    except Exception as e:
        rows.append((p.parent.parent.name,str(p.relative_to(root)),f'ERROR {e}'))
with open('engagement_snippets.txt','w') as f:
    for matter,path,snip in rows:
        f.write(f'### {matter} | {path}\n{snip}\n\n')
print('processed',len(rows))

# Top clients by number of matters

## Answer

I counted each unique matter folder (`documents/matters/<matter-number>/`) once and grouped the folders by the client relationship identified in the engagement or matter-administration documents. I did **not** count individual documents, drafts, closing letters, or scope-expansion letters as additional matters.

| Rank | Client / relationship | Matter count | Matter numbers |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 (tie) | **Lumos Analytics Inc.** | **10** | 1008-00001 through 1008-00010 |
| 1 (tie) | **Quorum Insurance Holdings Corp.** | **10** | 1025-00001 through 1025-00010 |
| 1 (tie) | **Cascade Retail Holdings Inc.** | **10** | 1038-00001 through 1038-00010 |
| 4 (tie) | **Dunmore Energy Holdings Ltd.** | **9** | 1016-00001 through 1016-00009 |
| 4 (tie) | **Aurelius Global Media Group PLC** | **9** | 1017-00001 through 1017-00009 |
| 4 (tie) | **Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp.** | **9** | 1018-00001 through 1018-00009 |

There is a three-way tie at the cutoff: the fifth-ranked position is shared by Dunmore, Aurelius, and Penterra. Accordingly, I have shown all six clients occupying the top-five rank positions rather than arbitrarily excluding one tied client.

## Reasoning and verification

1. I treated a matter as the unique matter-number directory, so multiple documents within one folder remained one matter.
2. I read the client-identification language in the engagement letters and related administrative/closing materials. The three 10-matter series consistently identify Lumos, Quorum, and Cascade, respectively.
3. I verified the 9-matter series similarly for Dunmore and Penterra. The Aurelius series includes parent-company, board, and subsidiary engagements, but the documents consistently identify the Aurelius relationship; those were counted once per matter folder.
4. As a cross-check, the workspace contains 266 unique matter folders. The highest folder-series counts are 10 for 1008, 1025, and 1038; 9 for 1016, 1017, and 1018; and no other series exceeds 8.
